newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares up,record kick-off to bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares up,record kick-off to bourse trade.

text.p: German DAX index hits new record high in early bourse trade at 4,452.28 points, with dealers saying that 4,500-point level could be reached over the day, although volumes are lower than in previous days.
At 0847 GMT the DAX stood at 4,451.96 points, up 30.24 points or 0.68 percent. The September DAX future earlier came within a whisker of 4,500 when it hit 4,498 points.
"We were a bit shaky at the beginning. Volumes are a little lower than in recent days, but I'm confident that we can reach 4,500 points at some stage over the day," a Frankfurt broker said.
Underpinning early gains was another successful overnight run on Wall Street with the Dow Jones Industrial Index closing around one percent higher at 8,254.89 points.

The dollar was slightly lower at 1.8326/31 marks, but stable and providing support. "I can't think of anything original to say anymore about the dollar and the German share market," one Frankfurt broker said.
"Daimler-Benz looks positive this morning and we are seeing good order flow ahead of their figures," he said.
However, Daimler's first-half figures came in at around expectations.

Operating profit in the first half rose to 1.849 billion marks compared to 827 million marks in the same period a year previously. The more-than-doubling of operating profit was pretty much in line with analysts' expectations.
Shares in Daimler fell 3.30 marks to 156 marks after the figures, which dealers said was mostly due to profit-taking, as the share had risen around nine percent already during the week.
Focus in early trade was on the financial sector. Among losers were banks Vereinsbank down 3.40 pct at 99.50 marks and Hypo-Bank down 1.10 marks at 76.50 marks.
Insurer Allianz AG Holding was down nearly two percent at 1,470 marks.

Earlier Vereinsbank detailed the terms of its planned merger with its fellow Bavarian bank Hypo-Bank. It said its offer to exchange on share in Allianz for six shares in Hypo-Bank would run from August 4 to September 10.

The utility sector was in favour as part of a sector rotation, dealers said, with the sector in need of some catch-up having trailed other sectors, notably the banks and the chemical companies, in the recent record-breaking run.
Veba AG was up 3.20 marks at 106.40 marks, Viag AG was up four marks at 793.50 marks and RWE AG was up 50 pfennigs at 81.60 marks.
